title: Four wheels
requestCopy: Anything on four wheels that starts every morning. I have almost no money. Please.
deliveredCopy: It starts. You have no idea what that means to me.
overdeliveredCopy: It starts AND the radio works? You're wasted on this town.

title: Won't strand her
requestCopy: My daughter drives forty minutes to college. Build me the car that never leaves her on the roadside.
deliveredCopy: I'll sleep now, I think. Thank you.
overdeliveredCopy: You checked things I didn't know cars had. I'm telling the whole neighbourhood.

title: The fleet spare
requestCopy: One of my drivers put cab twelve into a barrier and walked away laughing, so we're calling it a lucky week. I need a spare that starts every shift and forgives every driver. Nothing clever. Clever breaks.
deliveredCopy: She'll outlast three of my drivers. Come by {venue} on Thursday; tell the desk Numata stands for you.
overdeliveredCopy: Outlast three of my drivers? Give her a month, she'll outlast the fleet.

title: First proper car
requestCopy: I've saved up. I want a PROPER car this time, one I won't be embarrassed by, one that still starts every morning.
deliveredCopy: It's exactly what I meant and I never said what I meant.
overdeliveredCopy: My dad asked to drive it. My DAD.

title: Make it pull
requestCopy: Customer of mine wants a warm hatch, nothing silly, but it has to PULL. You find the base, you build it.
deliveredCopy: Clean work. It goes like it should.
overdeliveredCopy: You went past the brief. I respect that. So does the dyno.

title: The column clock
requestCopy: I'm writing about the pass again. Bring me something that clocks under the time printed in this column, and I'll put your garage's name in it.
deliveredCopy: Under the mark. The column runs next week; your name's in the last line.
overdeliveredCopy: WELL under. That's a headline, not a footnote.

title: The showroom standard
requestCopy: My forecourt sells the idea that a used car can be a new beginning. Bring me one I could photograph for the window, the kind that makes a young couple stop walking. I'll know it when I see it.
deliveredCopy: It'll photograph beautifully. Come to {venue}; the book at the door will have your name where mine used to be.
overdeliveredCopy: I didn't even need the photograph. She sold herself the moment she rolled onto the lot.

title: Low and loud
requestCopy: It needs to sit RIGHT. Low, wide, loud, and it still has to look like it means it when it's parked.
deliveredCopy: That stance. That's the one. We park up at the bay-side PA on Sunday nights. Bring something worth looking at and I'll tell them whose work it is.
overdeliveredCopy: People will stop walking when they see this. That's the whole point.

title: Street power, street manners
requestCopy: Real power, but it idles like a street car and my customer drives it to work. Both. No excuses.
deliveredCopy: Power AND manners. That's the hard one, and you did it. There's an editor at one of the tuning monthlies who still owes me a favour. Expect a phone call.
overdeliveredCopy: It made the number and then it just... idled. Beautiful.

title: Under one-fifteen
requestCopy: Last one. The big column. Under one-fifteen at Hakone, whatever it takes, and your garage is the name this town remembers.
deliveredCopy: That's the time. That's the story. Go read your own name.
overdeliveredCopy: You didn't beat the time, you erased it. Front page.

title: The quiet crate
requestCopy: Most of what I am offered is a story with a car attached. Bring me the other thing. Mint in every panel, nothing switched in, nothing dressed up as what it never was, and the papers saying exactly what the metal says. I read both.
deliveredCopy: The papers and the metal agree. That is rarer than it ought to be. Give them my name at the collector rooms; they will know it.
overdeliveredCopy: Not one part out of place. Not one number that disagrees with its own service book. I do not say that twice a year.
